# Build Log

Dated record of what was built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (building period 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-04).
Everything in this repository was created during the hackathon. Times are America/Los_Angeles.

**Pre-hackathon:** none of this repository's code existed before 2026-10-27. The author runs an existing market-data
product (DappGo); its code is not in this repository and is not part of this submission. Before the event the author only
read the participant guide and noted that DappGo's own AI-written stock commentary on 2026-10-26 failed its internal
fact-assertion check — the problem this project addresses.

Live run traces kept as evidence are in [`docs/evidence/`](docs/evidence/) (raw model responses, tool calls, token usage,
cost, latency; no API keys).

## Day 1 — 2026-10-27 (Tue)

Goal: confirm the Meta Model API, create the repo, make the first tool call against SEC EDGAR.

- Read the Meta Model API docs and the account's model list. Picked `muse-spark-1.3` (Responses API, function calling,
  structured output; $1.25 / $4.25 per 1M input/output tokens). Reasoning tokens count against `max_output_tokens`.
- Confirmed SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyfacts` access (requires a contact User-Agent).
- Created the repo (Python 3.12, uv, MIT).
- Built the EDGAR fact tool: ticker → CIK, metric aliases (companies switch XBRL concepts over time), period selection by
  dates rather than filing labels, quarter vs year-to-date separation, preference for 10-K/10-Q over other forms,
  `period_type` labels, and derived values when filings do not report them directly (Q4 = annual − 9-month YTD;
  cash-flow quarters = YTD differences). Every derived value lists its source filings. EPS and share counts are never
  derived.
- Built the agent loop: Muse Spark decomposes a claim into sub-claims and calls `lookup_fact` / `list_periods`
  (parallel calls), then returns a structured verdict. Python re-checks every cited number against the tool output;
  when the model and the program disagree, the program wins.
- Built a hard budget ledger: worst-case cost is reserved before every model call and the call is refused if it would
  exceed the budget; actual usage is reconciled afterwards.
- Every run writes a trace: requests, raw responses, tool calls/results, usage, cost, latency.
- First live smoke test: Muse Spark issued `lookup_fact(META, revenue, 2025Q2)` correctly (2.1 s, ~$0.002).
- First live end-to-end verification: "Meta's Q4 2024 revenue was $48.4 billion, and its full-year 2024 net income was
  $70 billion." → revenue **supported** ($48.385B, derived), net income **contradicted** ($62.36B from the 10-K);
  overall `contradicted`; model and program agreed. 3 model calls, $0.0173, 27.7 s.
- Found from the live trace: one turn came back `incomplete` (`max_output_tokens`). Added status checks, one retry with
  a doubled limit (budget-reserved), and a fail-closed `insufficient_evidence` result if still incomplete.
- Second live run: "Tesla's Q3 2025 net income was about $1.4 billion and Alphabet's Q4 2024 revenue exceeded
  $100 billion." → overall `contradicted` (Alphabet $96.469B), $0.019, 34 s. Exposed a gap: the program check only
  knows "equals within 1.5%", so "about $1.4B" vs $1.373B was a program mismatch while the model said supported, and
  "exceeded" was treated as equality. → Day 2.
- Spot-checked tool values against published results: META Q4 2024 revenue $48.385B, GOOG Q4 2024 revenue $96.469B,
  TSLA Q3 2025 net income $1.373B, META FY2024 net income $62.36B.
- Tests: 26 offline tests passing (fake model client, trimmed SEC fixtures).
- Commits: `7c5670b`, `97b5365`, `f0acc85`. Model spend today ≈ $0.04.

## Second provider: Muse Spark Open on Baseten — 2026-10-27

- Baseten Model APIs are OpenAI-compatible at `https://inference.baseten.co/v1`.
- The hackathon key works only with model id `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`.
- Chat Completions tool definitions use the nested OpenAI chat format; the
  smoke-test tool call returned `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and JSON-string
  function arguments, with tool results sent back as `role: "tool"` messages
  in the full stateless history.
- The model always reasons; reasoning text is returned in `reasoning_content`.
  `reasoning_effort=low` worked.
- Structured output and JSON mode are unavailable. Final verdicts must be
  requested as plain JSON, parsed, schema-validated, and repaired once on
  invalid output.
- Usage includes prompt/completion tokens, reasoning-token details, cached
  prompt-token details, and speculative accepted/rejected prediction-token
  details. Pricing is $1.25 input, $0.15 cached input, and $4.25 output per
  1M tokens.
- Rate-limit headers report 100 requests and 2,000,000 tokens; the Baseten
  credit pool is separate from the $150 Meta credit, with $100 Baseten credit.
- Live smoke test: tool call correct, 1.5 s, 666 input / 156 output tokens,
  52 reasoning tokens, ≈$0.0015.

## Day 2 scope — started 2026-10-27 (Tue) afternoon

Goal: make the program check understand how claims are phrased (approximate values, inequalities, growth rates).

- Added strict `compute_change` tool support with an optional prior-year base
  period, two underlying `lookup_fact` facts, absolute change, percentage
  change, and separate evidence IDs.
- Added pure number-phrase parsing with scale suffixes, percentage points, and
  precision derived from the last stated digit.
- Replaced expected/found program checks with claim-type and comparator-aware
  checks for values, inequalities, absolute changes, and percentage changes.
- Added model/program disagreement fields, program-derived overall verdict
  aggregation, offline parser/check tests, and replay coverage for the two
  live-trace claim shapes.
- Documented the tolerance rules in README.md.
- From the five 2026-10-27 live-run findings, accepted omitted, null, empty,
  `"null"`, and `"none"` `compute_change.base_period` values as the default
  prior-year period while retaining the required nullable strict-schema field.
- From the live change traces, resolved one `compute_change` citation together
  with its component fact IDs, deduplicated matching value evidence, and split
  `no_evidence` from `ambiguous_evidence`.
- Added direction-aware signed percentage/absolute-change checks, including
  `stated_sign_corrected`, and capped value tolerances at 10% of the stated
  magnitude.
- Built `history_rank` with quarter/annual windows, derived Q4 coverage,
  record-high/record-low and first-time-above sub-claims, plus `other` coverage
  sub-claims that remain unchecked.
- Resolved `first_time_above`, `record_high`, and `record_low` against one
  `history_rank` evidence window, using only periods through the claimed period
  and resolving phrase-only thresholds from matching sibling sub-claims.
- Added trimmed fixtures and fake-client replays for all five live traces,
  including the exact recorded `[E3, E4, E5]` citations, and expanded the
  offline suite to 90 passing tests.
- Lesson: replay tests now use recorded tool output verbatim.

## Evaluation set — 2026-10-27

- Built a 30-claim labeled evaluation set in `eval/claims.yaml` and generated
  `eval/claims.jsonl`, with 20 dev claims, 10 test claims, seven companies,
  value, rounding, inequality, growth, period, unit, multi-part, record/first,
  and SEC-insufficient-evidence categories.
- Added the independent raw-companyfacts gold builder
  `eval/build_gold.py`, which writes `eval/gold_facts.json` and
  `eval/GOLD_REVIEW.md`, including selected values, periods, accessions,
  concepts, and snapshot SHA-256 hashes.
- Added the sequential, resumable `single_shot` versus `agent` evaluation
  runner, shared budget accounting, pair result files, copied agent traces,
  budget-stop recording, and the `eval run` / `eval report` CLI commands.
- Completed the evaluation evidence ledger: single-shot traces now retain the
  rendered prompt and raw response, every pair records prompt hashes, timing,
  token buckets, model/tool calls and cost, and each run has a versioned
  manifest plus an auditable report. The first six-claim partial dev run was
  aborted by the author because its single-shot prompts/raw responses were not
  recorded; it is kept in `docs/evidence/eval-2026-10-27-aborted-partial/` as
  evidence and superseded by `eval-2026-10-27/`.
- Added offline fake-client tests for the independent gold builder, report
  metric math, no-tool single-shot requests, resume behavior, budget stops,
  dataset validation, and report generation.
- Live evaluation results will be added after the Claude Code live run.

### Live verification results (Muse Spark 1.3, 2026-10-27, traces in `docs/evidence/2026-10-27/`)

Five claims were run live before and after the Day 2 fixes. Program verdicts:

| Claim | Before fixes | After fixes | Actual (SEC) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta Q2 2025 revenue was $47.5B, up 22% YoY | insufficient (growth unchecked) | **supported** | $47.516B, +21.6% |
| Tesla Q3 2025 net income about $1.4B; Alphabet Q4 2024 revenue exceeded $100B | contradicted | **contradicted** (Tesla part supported) | $1.373B; $96.469B |
| Alphabet Q3 2025 revenue topped $100B for the first time | supported ("first time" silently ignored) | **supported**, both parts checked | $102.346B; no earlier quarter above $100B |
| Tesla revenue fell 10% YoY in Q3 2025 | insufficient (growth unchecked) | **contradicted** | +11.6% |
| Meta Q4 2026 revenue was $60B | insufficient | **insufficient_evidence** (not yet filed) | — |

Each run: 3–4 model calls, $0.015–0.029, 25–52 s. Two bugs were found only by live runs and fixed: the model passing
`"null"` as a string argument, and real `lookup_fact` output lacking the `period` field that a hand-trimmed test fixture
had. Offline suite: 98 tests. Model spend so far ≈ $0.29 (ledger in `runs/`, not committed).

## Documentation & visuals — 2026-10-27

- Added four Mermaid diagrams under `docs/diagrams/` and embedded them in `README.md`: the checking flow, a committed
  Alphabet real-run sequence, the model-versus-program decision, and the two provider paths.
- Added `docs/scripts/make_figures.py`, which rebuilds the before/after, verdict-card, and live cost/latency figures from
  this build log and the committed live traces without model calls or network access.
- Added SVG and PNG figures under `docs/figures/`; the optional evaluation figure is generated only when a complete
  `docs/evidence/eval-*/summary.json` exists.
- Added `docs/figures/hero.png`, an AI-generated illustration, and recorded its prompt in
  `docs/prompts/hero-image.md` (with a pointer left at `docs/figures/hero-prompt.md`).
- Restructured `README.md` for a short judge-facing read while retaining the run, EDGAR, provider, verdict, and
  evaluation details below the overview.
- Made every visual reproducible and reusable: added the evidence-hashed figure registry, offline `--all`/`--check` builder, `.mmd` diagram sources, README/VISUALS markers, and the prompt library with the exact hero prompt and variants.

## Evaluation runs, third provider, provenance and data checks — 2026-10-27 (Tue) evening

All runs below are committed under `docs/evidence/` with manifest, per-call traces (prompt, raw response, tokens incl.
reasoning, cost, latency) and `REPORT.md`. Gold labels for the 30 claims were committed before the first run
(`f54f5d6`).

- **Recording first.** A first dev run was stopped after 6 claims because single-shot prompts and raw responses were not
  being saved; it is kept as `eval-2026-10-27-aborted-partial/`. Added per-call traces for every system, a run manifest
  (commit, versions, prompt SHA-256s, data snapshot hashes, time window, ledger spend) and a `prompts/` registry that a
  test keeps in sync with the code.
- **Run 1 (dev, Meta API + Baseten).** Agents beat single-shot on accuracy (0.75 vs 0.60 / 0.40) but said "supported"
  for 3 false claims: the model chose `approx` for un-hedged numbers such as "$1.3 billion" (actual $1.373B). Also
  found: "Microsoft Q4 2025 $281.7B" is false under both fiscal and calendar readings but agents answered
  "insufficient"; one Meta API call failed with an expired `previous_response_id`.
  Fixes: the program infers the comparator from the claim's wording; both period readings are checked; the Meta path
  resends full history when a referenced response or reasoning item has expired.
- **Run 2 (dev agents + the held-out test split, first and only pre-registered test run).** False-supported fell to 0.
  Test accuracy: agent 7/10 (Meta API), 10/10 (Baseten); single-shot 5/10 and 3/10. Dev run exposed the Meta model
  writing free text into the `interpretations` field → only real evidence IDs are accepted.
- **Run 3 (post-hoc, agents on all 30).** Meta API agent 0.90 dev / 0.80 test, Baseten 0.95 / 1.00, still 0
  false-supported.
- **Third provider.** Added Muse Spark Open on Fireworks (`accounts/fireworks/models/muse-spark-open`) through a shared
  OpenAI-compatible chat adapter with its own budget pool. Its first live run cited the same Tesla fact twice under
  calendar and fiscal labels → identical evidence is now collapsed, and facts carry `fiscal_equals_calendar`.
- **Run 4 (all 30 claims, six systems, one code version).** Agent accuracy 30/30 on Baseten and Fireworks, 26/30 on the
  Meta API; single-shot 18/30 (Meta API), 10/30 (Fireworks), 6/30 (Baseten); 0 false-supported for every system.
  Paired agent − single-shot accuracy: +27 pts on Meta API (bootstrap 95% CI +7 to +47, McNemar p = 0.039), +79 on
  Baseten, +67 on Fireworks. Mean cost per claim $0.011–0.021; mean latency 10 s (Baseten agent) to 48 s (Fireworks
  agent). Two Baseten single-shot calls ended `incomplete` (reasoning used the whole output limit) and count as wrong.
- **Statistics in reports.** Wilson 95% intervals for accuracy, false-supported and insufficient rates (overall, per
  split, per category); paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seeded) and exact McNemar tests between systems.
- **Provenance.** Every fact now carries a tier (L1 audited 10-K, L2 reviewed 10-Q, L3 derived), confirming filings,
  revision status and a strength level; sub-claims and verdicts report the weakest evidence used. Added
  `sources/registry.yaml` and `docs/DATA_SOURCES.md` (what SEC XBRL covers and does not, claim-source tiers, and the rule
  that per-site reliability is only published with n ≥ 20 and a confidence interval).
- **Fiscal-label bug found while collecting real-world claims.** SEC companyfacts `fy`/`fp` describe the filing, not
  the period: Oracle's quarter ended 2026-08-31 is tagged `fy=2026` but is fiscal 2027 Q1. Both the verifier and the
  independent gold builder had relied on these fields, so they agreed with each other and were wrong together. Each now
  derives fiscal year and quarter from period dates and the issuer's fiscal year-end, with two separate
  implementations; they agree on all 159,368 quarterly, year-to-date and annual facts since 2019 for 23 issuers, and
  match the issuers' own quarter names (Oracle, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Tesla). The 30 v1 gold verdicts were
  unchanged.
- **SEC tagging errors.** A data-quality checker over 24 issuers (`docs/DATA_QUALITY.md`) found that Oracle's 10-Ks filed
  in 2020–2022 tag full-year revenue for fiscal 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022 on the fourth-quarter period. The verifier
  now drops a quarter whose value equals its covering annual value, derives the quarter instead (Oracle FY2018 Q4:
  $11.0B rather than $39.4B) and lists the excluded row. A first version flagged any quarter above 60% of the year; it
  produced 154 false alarms (e.g. Tesla's Q4 2012 revenue really was 74% of that year) and was replaced by the exact-match
  rule, which flags only the 6 Oracle rows. The checker reports 21 consistency anomalies and 603 revised periods (289
  above 0.5%); revisions are listed separately because later filings routinely reclassify earlier periods.
- **Eval v2 in progress.** A seeded generator (`eval/v2/`) builds 260 claims across 23 companies and 10 families,
  including 26 deliberately ambiguous fiscal/calendar claims whose gold is computed under both readings. Review of the
  first draft found wrong month names, missing years and an "at least" claim worded as an equality; these were fixed
  before freezing.
- **Figures.** The evaluation chart now shows all six systems with Wilson intervals; added a data-quality chart and
  Fireworks to the provider diagram.

## Eval v2 run: 357 claims × 6 systems — 2026-10-27 (Tue) night (UTC 2026-10-28 03:09–06:27)

- **Run size.** Ran the frozen v2 set (commit `5d90b3b`) on all six systems: 2,142 verdicts. Concurrency 6, per-provider budget cap. Report: [`docs/evidence/eval-v2-2026-10-27/REPORT.md`](docs/evidence/eval-v2-2026-10-27/REPORT.md).
- **Budget stop and resume.**
  - Meta API spend reached the $15 per-provider cap with 95 Meta pairs left (48 agent, 47 single-shot); the other providers finished.
  - The owner raised the cap to $30.
  - The 95 `budget_stopped` pair files and the first report were moved to `budget-stopped-attempt1/`, kept as evidence, and only those pairs were rerun. The ledger continued, so spend is cumulative.
- **Results (corrected gold).** 95% CIs in brackets.

  | System | Accuracy |
  | --- | --- |
  | Agent, Baseten | 90.5% [87.0, 93.1] |
  | Agent, Fireworks | 90.5% [87.0, 93.1] |
  | Agent, Meta API | 83.2% [79.0, 86.7] |
  | Single-shot, Meta API | 44.3% [39.2, 49.4] |
  | Single-shot, Baseten | 20.7% |
  | Single-shot, Fireworks | 19.9% |

  - **Paired agent − single-shot:** +38 (Meta API), +70 (Baseten), +70 (Fireworks) points; McNemar p < 0.0001 for each.
  - **Open-weights agent vs hosted agent:** +7 points, p = 0.0001.
- **Real-world layer (43 claims).** Agent 43/43 on Baseten and Fireworks, 39/43 on the Meta API; single-shot 6/43.
- **Weak families:**
  - "First time / record" claims: 16–18 of 31 right.
  - Year-over-year on the Meta API agent: 29/48 (Baseten and Fireworks: 45/48).
  - Fiscal/calendar period traps: 23–24 of 30.
- **Cost of this run.** Meta API $15.67, Baseten $11.42, Fireworks $11.35, from ledger reconcile events. Mean per claim: agent $0.020–0.026, single-shot $0.012–0.019.
- **Review of every false "supported" verdict.** Found two bugs:
  1. **Gold builder: Amazon treated as a June year-end issuer.** It read the latest "annual" end from facts labeled `FY`. After period relabeling, that included a 10-Q trailing-twelve-month net income (2025-04-01..2026-03-31).
     - Two true claims had been labeled "contradicted": G0119 (Amazon calendar Q3 2023 revenue $143.1B) and G0125 (EPS $0.94).
     - **Fix:** in both the gold builder and `claimcheck.fiscal`, 12-month periods that do not end at a fiscal year-end are labeled `TTM`. A relabeled "fiscal label as calendar" trap is only false for a non-calendar issuer.
     - **Impact:** v1 gold is unchanged (30/30), and only those 2 v2 claims change.
     - **Record:** the frozen file is left as committed. The corrections, with reasons, are in `eval/v2/claims-v2-corrected.jsonl`. Both reports are kept: `REPORT.md` (corrected) and `REPORT-registered-gold.md`. Every system's correct count moves by ≤ 2.
  2. **Lookup tool: Apple's 52/53-week quarter put in the wrong calendar quarter.** The quarter ending 2023-07-01 was mapped to calendar Q3, because a derived (YTD-difference) quarter has no SEC frame and fell back to the end-date month.
     - G0249 ("2023 Q3 net income $19.9B") was then judged supported by all three agents.
     - **Fix:** the calendar quarter is taken from the end date minus 7 days, matching SEC frames (CY2023Q2).
     - **Status:** post-hoc. This run was not re-scored with the fix.
- **Remaining agent false "supported".** Meta API agent on two "Q2/Q4 2024"-style claims for non-calendar issuers (NVIDIA, Apple). It checked only the fiscal reading, and gold is "insufficient evidence" because the readings disagree.
  - **Next:** have the program detect an unlabeled quarter for a non-calendar issuer and require both readings.
- **Tests and figures.** Added regression tests for the TTM label and the 52/53-week calendar quarter (192 tests pass). Regenerated `docs/figures/eval-summary.*` from the v2 summary.

## Day 3 — 2026-10-28 (Wed)

- **Results explorer.** [`docs/explorer/`](docs/explorer/) shows six-system accuracy with CIs, per-family heatmap, and every claim's six verdicts, the program's decision steps and the cited SEC filing. Data comes from `docs/scripts/build_explorer_data.py`.
- **Post checking.** New `python -m claimcheck post` (module `claimcheck.post`, prompt `prompts/post-extraction.md`).
  - Muse Spark extracts claims with an exact quote. The program accepts a claim only if the quote is a span of the post and every number in the rewrite appears in it. Years and quarters may come from elsewhere in the post.
  - Forecasts and opinions are labeled, not verified. Output is `report.json` plus a highlighted `report.html`.
- **Bug: growth multipliers.** First live run, English thread on Baseten: NVIDIA "fiscal 2024 revenue … more than double the year before" came back contradicted, although the actual figure is +125.9%.
  - **Cause:** "more than double" has no digits. The parser found no number, the comparator inference fell back to `eq`, and that overrode the model's correct `gt`.
  - **Fix:** growth multipliers are rewritten as percent growth before parsing. "more than double" → `gt 100%`. A bare "doubled" → `approx 100%` with ±15% of the implied rate. "tripled" → 200%.
  - **Rerun:** 4/4 checkable claims right. The before-fix run is kept as `bigtech-thread-baseten-before-multiplier-fix/`.
- **Bug: Chinese 億 units.** First Chinese run on the Meta API: the extraction translated 億 literally ("500 hundred million US dollars"), and the parser read it as $500 million. That made a false Coca-Cola "revenue over 500 億美元" claim supported; actual 2024 revenue was $47.06B.
  - **Fix:** the extraction prompt converts 億/萬 to billion/thousand, and the program also rewrites any literal "hundred million" / "ten thousand" before verification.
  - **Rerun:** Microsoft FY2024 supported, Coca-Cola contradicted, Meta "623 億" contradicted (filed $62.36B rounds to 624 億). The before-fix run is kept.
- **Tests.** 199 pass, including 9 new ones for screening, scale words and multipliers.
- **Spend.** Post runs: about $0.07 (Baseten) and $0.09–0.10 per run (Meta API). The per-provider budget cap was raised to $60 by the owner.
- **Fix: ambiguous quarters (commit `102b20c`).** A claim like "Q2 2024" with no fiscal/calendar label, for a non-calendar issuer, now makes the program fetch the reading the model did not check (evidence IDs `P*`). If the two readings disagree, the verdict is insufficient evidence. Implemented by Codex, reviewed; 215 tests pass.
- **Post-hoc agent rerun (UTC 21:07–22:49).** The three agents on all 357 claims with the corrected gold, $60 cap per provider; single-shot was not rerun (its code path is unchanged), so its rows in this report read 0 and are not results. Evidence: `docs/evidence/eval-v2-2026-10-28-r2-posthoc/`.
  - Fireworks 329/357 = 92.2% (v2 90.5%), Baseten 325/357 = 91.0% (90.5%), Meta API 305/357 = 85.4% (83.2%).
  - False "supported" 0/186 for all three (v2: 1, 1, 4). G0235/G0240/G0249 moved to insufficient evidence.
  - Paired flips vs v2 (fixed/broke): Fireworks 9/3, Baseten 8/6, Meta API 27/19; McNemar p = 0.15, 0.79, 0.30, so accuracy changes are within noise.
  - Meta API: 3 provider errors (two 400 "No tool output found for function call", one 503), counted wrong.
  - Spend: Meta $8.96, Baseten $7.23, Fireworks $7.31. Labeled post-hoc: fixes were designed after seeing v2 failures.
- **Media production (Day 3 evening).** Website "See filing" pop-up and post-hoc rerun block shipped; stamp animation
  in review; X thread and Discord intro posted; demo video v001 → v002 built with local Breeze-TTS-2 narration
  (one locked voice), ACE-Step music and an HTML/JS motion timeline under staged Owner approval and a second-AI
  review. Full record: [docs/PROCESS-media.md](docs/PROCESS-media.md).

## Day 4 — 2026-10-29 (Thu)

- **L4 earnings-release evidence.** Built during the hackathon: Item 2.02 8-K discovery from SEC submissions, filing-index Ex 99.1/HTML Ex 99.2 retrieval, raw-byte caches with verified SHA-256, and a SEC fair-access gate shared with XBRL (nine request starts/second; contact User-Agent retained).
- **Deterministic extraction and checks.** New modules parse normalized text and table coordinates, including colspan/rowspan, explicit fiscal/calendar periods, displayed units, negative values, numeric ranges and literal plus/minus widths. The Meta agent selects a quote through strict find/quote tools. Python re-extracts the span and numbers from the cached bytes at selection and final checking; model-supplied numbers never decide the verdict. Missing outlook, unsupported verbal bounds, wrong period/unit/issuer, YTD/TTM and conflicting candidates fail closed. Guidance/non-GAAP cannot be relabeled as ordinary GAAP values to bypass the check.
- **Release and filing precedence.** For reported consolidated totals, exact-period L1/L2 XBRL wins a conflict and adds `release_vs_filing_mismatch`, retaining both citations. L4 is furnished, unaudited and medium strength at most. Report JSON retains accession, exhibit URL, filed date, hash, exact quote and highlight offsets; HTML renders the numeric highlight. Issuer guidance enters post verification, while third-party forecasts remain outside it.
- **Gold before model calls.** Recorded eight real SEC release source chains (AAPL, ADBE, AMD, AMZN, CRM, INTC, META, NVDA), plus explicitly trimmed XBRL replay snapshots. Independent `eval/l4/build_gold.py` uses manual table/column coordinates or literal sentence anchors and Decimal, with no runtime verifier imports or model calls. Registered 32 claims: 13 supported, 10 contradicted perturbations, nine insufficient. Gold commit `88ad316` precedes every model call; runtime commit `3530800` freezes the evaluated code. This is a regression benchmark developed alongside its fixtures, not a blinded holdout.
- **Local commits and environment.** The managed sandbox blocks the shared main-checkout `.git`, so commits use `/private/tmp/market-claim-verifier-l4-local.git` on the requested feature branch from `f06ac10`, with a portable bundle for Claude. The eval verifies those real committed bytes through `--git-dir`. No push. Shared `.venv`/`.cache` symlinks are excluded, and pytest imports this worktree's `src` rather than the virtualenv's other-worktree editable install. Staged files were checked for actual configured key values and credential patterns before each commit; no keys printed or stored.
- **Validation and eval.** Full suite before the live run: 325 passed. The Baseten-only Meta Muse Spark Open run uses one $5 ledger, disabled SDK retries, immutable gold/code, and offline SEC replay. Exact results and retained failures are recorded in [the L4 evidence directory](docs/evidence/eval-l4-2026-10-29/REPORT.md).
- **L4 live result.** One Baseten run: 31/32 = 96.9% (Wilson 95% CI 84.3–99.4%); false-supported 0/19 (Wilson 0–16.8%); $0.71569815, 131 requests, median 10.6 s / p95 28.3 s. No provider errors or budget stops. The one supported-to-insufficient miss is a model query-kind mismatch for META free cash flow; it remains in the score and traces, with no gold edits or score-selected model rerun.
- **Post-run final review.** Added fail-closed numeric-token/negative-sign guards and refused ambiguous parallel GAAP/non-GAAP points. Insufficient reports retain inspected SEC release links. A regression guard prevents Target's issuer name from being interpreted as a guidance keyword. These changes are explicitly post-run; an offline replay of the original model responses and tool arguments preserves all 32 verdicts without new model calls. See [analysis and limitations](docs/evidence/eval-l4-2026-10-29/ANALYSIS.md).
- **Final verification.** `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`: 341 passed. Offline replay: 32/32 verdicts unchanged, zero new model calls. Prompt exports are synchronized; secret scans include configured key values and credential patterns. Every successful assemble exports the next `demo/out/demo-vNNN.mp4` and matching `.srt`, writes a complete

consume a version number. An unchanged assemble reuses its master but records a new export version.

The deliverable is **1920×1080, 30 fps, H.264 + AAC, at most 180 seconds**. The storyboard's 170 seconds is a
soft target. Each scene lasts measured narration + 0.6 seconds, rounded up to a video frame; adjacent scenes
overlap by 0.4 seconds. Consequently total length is the sum of scene lengths minus 0.4 × (scene count − 1).
The overlap consumes silent padding, never speech. A scene more than 25% over its target gets a warning.
An export over three minutes is rejected; narration is never automatically rewritten or accelerated.

## Local tools and offline dependencies

Python dependencies are exact pins in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. Python 3.14 is selected by `.python-version`
(the project supports 3.12–3.14). FFmpeg and ffprobe are `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe`.
Use Node with an already-installed Playwright **1.64.x** and its Chromium. The scripts look in normal Node
resolution, `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`, and existing `~/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/playwright` directories.
For another existing installation, set `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to the absolute Playwright package directory.
The builder never runs npm/npx installation or downloads Chromium.

This working copy has a self-contained dependency cache populated from local wheels. To keep uv entirely
offline and its writes inside the demo scope:

```sh
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/demo/cache/uv"
export UV_OFFLINE=1
uv sync --project demo --locked
node demo/capture/browser.mjs --version
uv run --project demo pytest demo/tests --basetemp=demo/cache/pytest -q
```

Prepare any missing tools/dependencies on the host before building in a restricted environment. Browser
contexts allow only `https://yanlonglai.github.io/market-claim-verifier/…`, block service workers and WebSockets,
and abort other requests. Filing links are displayed but never followed to sec.gov. The card uses local HTML
and system fonts. This run made no package/model downloads.

### Apply the v002 director's fixes on the host

The reviewed v001 export and run record are already present. From this worktree, run only capture and
assemble; narration, music, generated stills, and the rendered end card reuse their existing caches:

```sh
cd /Users/yan/git/market-claim-verifier-demo
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/demo/cache/uv"
export UV_OFFLINE=1
uv run --project demo python demo/build.py capture --storyboard demo/storyboard-v1.yaml && uv run --project demo python demo/build.py assemble --storyboard demo/storyboard-v1.yaml
```

No `--force`, `voice`, or `card` run is needed. Capture settings and script changes invalidate all seven
capture keys; the caption layout change invalidates the rendered scene clips during assemble. With v001
as the latest successful export, this writes `demo/out/demo-v002.mp4`, its SRT, and a new run record.
Chromium must run on the host. Review all seven captures there, particularly the three cards in s05 and the
highlighted table row in s06. The framing checks fail if the chart, cards, or filing table extend into the
caption bands. The full scene changes are listed below.

`all` executes voice → capture → card → assemble; assembly validates the externally supplied stills.
Every command accepts `--force`, `--only SCENE` (repeat or comma-separate), `--voice-fallback say`, and
`--storyboard PATH`. `--only` limits generation/rendering. Assembly always includes the entire storyboard and
requires current caches for unselected scenes; make an initial full build first. Keep the same voice settings
between stage commands. `--force all --only …` refreshes that scene and the final mix. A process lock prevents
two CLI builds from writing the same caches or export number concurrently.

Cache directories are `cache/<stage>/<scene-id>/<content hash>/`. Receipts hash the actual artifacts as well
as their inputs, so damaged files are regenerated. Voice keys are SHA-256 of a canonical JSON tuple containing
the actual engine, instruction, seed, and narration with whitespace collapsed. Each scene has independent
voice, visual, and rendered-scene keys. Music has its own global key. Editing one scene leaves other scenes'
voice/capture/render caches reusable; only the final joined master must change. Previous hash directories
remain available if an edit is reverted. Use `--force capture` after a live site update: live page contents are
not fetched merely to check cache validity.

## Narration, music, and captions

Breeze is invoked once for the pending clips, reusing its loaded model:

```text
/Users/yan/ml-engines/breeze-tts/run.sh --device auto --jobs <jobs.json> --instruction <storyboard.voice.instruction> --seed <storyboard.voice.seed>
```

Jobs are `{id,text,out}` with absolute output paths under `cache/voice/`. Each `<out>.json` engine receipt is
read and preserved. Audio is validated, converted to 24 kHz mono WAV, and measured with ffprobe. Breeze's
installed `INSTALL.md` and `tts.py` define the batch interface. Its per-clip seed reset makes cached single-scene
regeneration independent of batch order. Missing Breeze fails unless `--voice-fallback say` was explicitly
provided. A runtime synthesis failure is reported; the fallback is not silently selected for such failures.

The draft fallback invokes macOS `say -v Samantha`, converts its AIFF output to 24 kHz mono WAV, and records
engine `macos-say`, `draft_only: true`. macOS say cannot honor Breeze's male voice instruction or seed; the
receipt says so. If the sandbox produces a zero-frame AIFF, the builder rejects it. For a deliberate Samantha
draft while Breeze is installed, explicitly set `voice.engine: say` in a separate storyboard and pass
`--storyboard demo/<draft-storyboard>.yaml`.

The music prompt is `prompts/music/bed.md`. Music is generated separately by Claude on the host, never by this
builder. The current host-generated `cache/music/bed-seed92.wav` is available. The exact ACE-Step regeneration
command, from the repository root, uses a fresh output name because the engine refuses to overwrite:

```sh
/Users/yan/git/number-rpg/audio/engines/ace-step/run.sh \
  --prompt 'minimal modern tech documentary underscore, soft electric piano, warm analog synth pad, light muted plucks, gentle kick on half-time, 92 bpm, D major, calm and confident, no drops, no vocals, instrumental' \
  --lyrics '[instrumental]' \
  --duration 190 --seed 92 --infer-steps 60 --guidance-scale 15 \
  --out "$PWD/demo/cache/music/bed-seed92-rerender.wav"
```

The wrapper pins its local checkpoint and uses MPS, float32, Euler/APG, with BF16 disabled. Follow the prompt's
notes when reviewing the result: it must sit under speech, without a lead melody in the voice band or sudden
swells. Set `music.path: demo/cache/music/bed-seed92.wav` in the storyboard to pin a bed; otherwise the newest
`cache/music/bed-*.wav` by modification time is selected and its SHA-256 is recorded. With no bed, the builder
announces that it is exporting narration only. It loops/trims music to length, applies `music.gain_db`, ducks
it with narration sidechain compression, and fades the bed out over the last two seconds. Two-pass loudnorm
targets −14 LUFS; the encoded AAC is then measured again and must be within 0.5 LU of that target with true
peak ≤ −1 dBTP. A true-peak margin accounts for AAC overshoot.

Subtitles preserve narration and are split into at most two lines of at most 42 characters. Their timing is
word-weighted within each measured voice clip; this is an estimate, so listen during review. Scene offsets
account for crossfades. Identical cues are burned in and exported as SRT. Pillow renders readable system-font
PNG panels because the supplied ffmpeg has no libass/drawtext filters; FFmpeg composites them. The scene
label (lower third) fades in/out at the top-left, 64 px from both edges. Subtitles stay bottom-centre,
66 px from the bottom, with white type, navy panels, and mint accents.

# Live check and visible agent trace

Implementation and operator handoff, updated 2026-11-03. The owner-selected runtime is Python 3.12 on DappGo's x86_64 k3s host, reached through Cloudflare Tunnel and Access from **free Pages Functions**. This document does not mean the endpoint is deployed. [Exact host, Tunnel, Access and Pages steps](../deploy/README.md). No paid model call is needed to build or test this change.

## Architecture and verdict identity

The browser posts `{ "text": "…", "password": "…", "provider": "baseten" }` to same-origin `/api/check`; provider is optional and defaults to Baseten. The [Pages Function](../functions/api/check.ts) validates the request and forwards only these fields, trusted `CF-Connecting-IP` as `X-Live-Client-IP`, and at most 1,024 User-Agent characters for history parsing to `https://${LIVE_ORIGIN_HOST}/api/check`. It supplies `CF-Access-Client-Id`, `CF-Access-Client-Secret` and `X-Live-Origin-Token` from server-side configuration. Visitor cookies, Authorization and other browser headers are not forwarded. Redirects are disabled; a 25-second abort includes response-body reading. Invalid origin responses fail closed to the saved demo; public result fields and budget counters are allowlisted.

The [self-hosted adapter](../server/live/server.py) authenticates **every route**, including `/healthz`, against `LIVE_ORIGIN_TOKEN` using a fixed-size constant-time digest comparison. Missing tokens return 401; wrong tokens return 403. It then authenticates check/compare passwords before budgets, rate limits, SEC or model I/O. Routes are `GET /api/budget`, `POST /api/check`, `POST /api/check-example`, `POST /api/compare`, `GET /api/history`, `GET /api/history/{id}`, and `GET /healthz`. History and budget reads need no review password. The browser receives no provider key.

The adapter imports the [gate](../workers/live/src/gate.py), [runner](../workers/live/src/live.py) and claimcheck Python modules directly. The [image](../server/live/Dockerfile) copies these sources, not a TypeScript port. Fact selection, fiscal normalization, calculations, evidence IDs, strict JSON parsing and final evaluation remain Python. A model proposal cannot override a program verdict: any contradiction → `contradicted`; every extracted assertion supported → `supported`; otherwise → `insufficient_evidence`. Individual checks may remain `unchecked`. Missing explicit dated periods abstain without a model call. Extraction can miss assertions; a supported result applies to the assertions actually extracted. SEC evidence can be incomplete or restated.

[Recorded replay tests](../tests/test_live_check.py) reproduce the three Apple Baseten responses, including malformed JSON/repair, and compare all **357 v2 Baseten saved tool transcripts** through live finish and CLI evaluation. Those old companyfacts-only records explicitly treat unavailable earnings-release fallback evidence as unavailable; they do not fetch or synthesize L4 evidence. This is a frozen-response recheck, not a new model evaluation, OCR/ASR test or accuracy measurement. [Server adapter tests](../tests/test_live_server.py) replay Apple through fake HTTP transports and real SQLite.

## Provider receipts, compare and history

Provider IDs are exactly `baseten`, `fireworks`, and `meta`. The runner reuses the [existing adapters and pricing](../src/claimcheck/providers.py) with fixed models `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, `accounts/fireworks/models/muse-spark-open`, and `muse-spark-1.3`, respectively. Unknown providers return 400 / `unknown_provider` before reservation. Meta OCR/ASR preprocessing is independent of the verifier choice; each paid call reserves from the same durable ledger before network I/O. Missing/invalid usage retains the conservative hold, reflected by `cost_is_bound`.

JSON POST bodies are at most 1 KiB, including chunked bodies. Extra request keys, query strings and cross-origin browser requests are rejected. Routes accept exactly:

```text
POST /api/check         {text, password, provider?}
POST /api/check-example {example_id, password, provider?}
POST /api/compare       {text, password, providers:[provider, provider, provider?]}
                    or {example_id, password, providers:[provider, provider, provider?]}
GET  /api/history?limit=50
GET  /api/history/{id}
```

Compare requires 2–3 distinct providers and returns `{ "runs": [envelope, …] }` in request order. Each member checks budget before starting and reserves before each paid call. A budget, lifetime, credit or rate stop ends the sequence; the final attempted member is an error envelope. Completed and failed members are retained separately. Other provider failures allow the next provider to run. The shared per-IP rate counter counts each member. Compare authentication/validation errors use the ordinary error response; an accepted comparison returns HTTP 200 even when a member fails.

Every live run envelope, including a failed attempt, adds these fields (numeric values below are illustrative, not measurements):

```json
{
  "receipt": {
    "provider": "baseten",
    "model": "meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026",
    "latency_ms": 6300,
    "cost_usd": 0.0099,
    "preprocessing": null
  },
  "input": {"kind": "text", "text_read": "Apple FY2025 revenue was $416.2B."}
}
```

`receipt.cost_usd` and `receipt.latency_ms` cover verification. Media examples have `preprocessing: {"model":"muse-voice-transcribe-1.0","latency_ms":1200,"cost_usd":0.001}` (model depends on input kind). Native text/PDF examples use `native-text` / `native-pdf` with zero preprocessing cost. Pasted text uses `null`. Top-level `cost_usd` and `latency_ms` include preprocessing; their values equal the sum of the two receipt portions. Costs are USD estimates or retained upper bounds, not provider invoice amounts.

`input` is `{kind, example_id?, story?, text_read}`. `kind` is `text|image|pdf|audio|video`, and `story` is `a|b|c`. Original unprefixed IDs (`text` through `video`) mean story A; prefixed IDs (`a-text` through `c-video`) are supported when packaged as ready, hash-matching entries. W1 does not create the other stories' assets. Example inputs also retain the existing `input.preprocessing: {model, provider, latency_ms, cost_usd}` for compatibility; receipt preprocessing has exactly the three fields above. Media `text_read` may contain at most 12,000 characters; the public row keeps only its first 600.

`GET /api/history` returns `{ "rows": [row, …] }`, newest first. `limit` defaults to 50 and accepts a single integer from 1 to 50; duplicate/unknown query keys are rejected. Summary rows have exactly this shape:

```json
{
  "id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "at": "2026-11-04T01:00:00.000Z",
  "ip_masked": "192.0.*.*#1234abcd",
  "device": "Windows / desktop",
  "browser": "Edge",
  "kind": "text",
  "example_id": null,
  "story": null,
  "input_text": "Apple FY2025 revenue was $416.2B.",
  "provider": "baseten",
  "model": "meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026",
  "verdict": "supported",
  "corrections_count": 0,
  "latency_ms": 6300,
  "cost_usd": 0.0099,
  "preprocessing_cost_usd": 0
}
```

`GET /api/history/{id}` returns the same row plus `envelope`, the retained public run envelope (≤65,536 serialized bytes). Unknown, expired or pruned IDs return 404 / `not_found`; malformed IDs return 400. Failed attempts have `verdict: null` and normally zero corrections. `corrections_count` counts edits in the original result. When an envelope is too large, `history_truncated: true` marks removal of trailing trace/evidence/claim items; the receipt and input are retained, with input limited to 600 characters if needed and corrections omitted as a last resort. Such a reopened result is partial. History responses are `no-store` and pass strict row/receipt/input allowlists, including on detail reads.

History resides in `/data/ledger.sqlite3` on the existing PVC. Only authenticated, validated attempts are stored, including paid failures, budget/rate stops and each compare member; authentication and input-validation rejections create no row. Retention is 14 days and at most 5,000 rows, enforced on insert and by the existing 60-second periodic prune. Reads immediately exclude expired rows. IPv4 retains only its first two octets and an eight-hex keyed hash; IPv6 uses its first two hextets, and invalid/missing addresses become `unknown`. The private hash salt persists across restarts. User-Agent is reduced to deterministic browser family plus OS/device class by a small parser, with no external UA library; raw IP and UA are never retained. [Provider/history tests](../tests/test_live_providers_history.py) and [Pages contract tests](../tests/node/live-v3-boundary.test.mjs) use fake transports and temporary SQLite, not fresh provider or OCR/ASR execution.

## Corrected draft

Successful checks also return `corrections`, generated by the pure Python [correction builder](../src/claimcheck/correction.py). The site labels it **Corrected draft — only listed assertions checked / 修正版草稿——僅核對列出的主張**. This is a partial draft, never article approval. No extra model call is made and no model rewrite, summary or proposed replacement supplies its numbers.

The corrections object contains `original_text`, `span_unit: "unicode_codepoints"`, ordered `edits`, and `not_corrected` records with English/繁中 reasons. Supported assertions get `supported` (no edit needed), unchecked opinions/out-of-scope assertions get `not_judged`, and insufficient evidence gets `insufficient_evidence` (not corrected). Single-assertion inputs and the [saved Apple demo](site/data/live-demo.json) also include this object. Each edit includes `start`, `end`, `original`, `replacement`, program `actual_value`, evidence `unit`, `period`, optional `base_period`, `evidence_ids` and `citations`. The replacement preserves the original scale, precision and grouping, using decimal half-up rounding. Examples include `$416.2B` → `$102.5B` and `4162億美元` → `1025億美元`.

Directly below the draft, the site states: “Only the assertions listed below were checked; nothing else in the text was verified.” / 「僅核對下方列出的主張；文中其餘內容均未經查證。」

An edit needs a unique literal assertion or unique original number, matching stated units and periods, a finite contradicted program value and complete SEC citations. The original context must identify the checked issuer and financial metric uniquely; a matching number cannot move a revenue fact onto a cash assertion or another company. If a model normalized the assertion's wording, the unique number must bind within an original sentence with the checked period. Duplicate or overlapping spans, missing evidence or component citations, unresolved periods, inequalities, ranges, compound amounts and qualitative claims such as “first ever” retain their original text and receive a reason under **Not corrected / 未修正**. Directional growth can substitute a magnitude only when the verified direction agrees with the original wording. Supported assertions remain unchanged. The draft cannot cover assertions extraction missed.

For derived results without a top-level `filing_url`, the builder recursively cites every component filing, reconstructing SEC archive links from recorded CIK/accession metadata when necessary. It never fetches a filing. The saved [Apple revenue case](evidence/posts-2026-10-28/demo-thread-baseten/report.json) yields:

> Apple pulled in ~~$416.2 billion~~ → **$102.5 billion** of revenue in fiscal Q4 2025 alone.

Its [retained trace](evidence/posts-2026-10-28/demo-thread-baseten/traces/20261029T023240Z-12ac28b8.json) records $416.161B annual minus $313.695B nine-month revenue, yielding $102.466B. Both recorded component filings are cited; this offline recheck does not revalidate them against today's SEC data. [Correction tests and validation records](evidence/corrected-draft-2026-11-03/REPORT.md) cover the retained case, span binding, units/periods, citations and hostile-text rendering. The site uses text nodes, `<del>` and `<strong>` and converts code-point offsets explicitly, including emoji. Pages passes corrections through its public allowlist. No separate model rewrite or budget action is needed for corrections.

## Limits and failure behavior

| Limit | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Input | 1–600 Unicode characters after trimming; 1 KiB JSON body ceiling, including chunked bodies |
| Password | `LIVE_CHECK_PASSWORD` from env/file; missing/empty disables checks with 503; missing/wrong input returns 401 before reservation/model I/O |
| Failed passwords | Five failures per IP per 15 minutes, then 429 for 15 minutes from the fifth failure; correct passwords remain blocked during lockout; other IPs independent |
| Scope | US SEC issuers and companyfacts; at most three issuers; no prices, investment advice, crypto, forecasts, non-GAAP or issuer-release verification |
| Calls | At most four model calls, 2,000 output tokens each; at most six tool calls; no automatic provider retry |
| Time | 28-second text / 60-second example run; 22-second verifier/SEC and 50-second Meta preprocessing I/O; Pages: 25-second text / 65-second example / 195-second compare; browser timing belongs to the site; no measured production SLA |
| Rate | Five accepted checks per IP per ten minutes; raw IP never stored |
| Daily spend | `DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, deployment $10 per UTC day; zero disables calls; invalid/negative/nonfinite values fail closed |
| Lifetime spend | `TOTAL_BUDGET_USD`, deployment $60 across all days; lack of reservation room latches a stop |
| Provider credit | 402, or 403/429 with credit/payment/quota exhaustion wording, durably pauses calls; ordinary auth/rate errors do not latch a credit stop |
| SEC cache | Six-hour memory/disk cache of successful JSON bodies only; HTTPS host allowlist `www.sec.gov` / `data.sec.gov`; redirects disabled |

SEC requests use exactly `User-Agent: DappGo market-claim-verifier admin@dappgo.com`. Tool arguments cannot supply fetch URLs. [Pages routes](_routes.json) include `/api/check`, `/api/check-example`, `/api/compare`, `/api/history`, `/api/history/*` and `/api/budget`. The [CSP](_headers), language switch, color schemes, cache-busted assets and reduced-motion behavior remain in use.

Provider errors, incomplete/model-invalid responses, SEC failures and timeouts issue no financial verdict. Reserved costs remain accounted for and available partial steps are shown. Daily exhaustion returns 429 / `budget_exhausted`; lifetime/provider stops return 503 / `total_budget_exhausted` or `credit_exhausted`. Rate limits return 429; timeouts return 504 / `timeout` from Python. Missing origin configuration, unavailable counters or absent keys fail closed to the saved demo.

## Public remaining-budget display

`GET /api/budget` uses [the budget Function](../functions/api/budget.ts) and the same persistent ledger as checks. Visitors need no review password to read the aggregate; Pages still authenticates to Access and the origin. The [boundary](../workers/pages/check.mjs) returns only:

```json
{"day":"2026-11-02","daily_limit_usd":10.0,"daily_spent_usd":0.59,"daily_remaining_usd":9.41,"resets_at":"2026-11-03T00:00:00Z","status":"ready"}
```

Status is `ready`, `budget_exhausted`, `total_budget_exhausted` or `credit_exhausted`. This is an application allowance, not the provider balance. Successful responses allow five seconds of shared caching; errors are `no-store`. A visitor request with `Cache-Control: no-cache` receives `no-store` and a fresh ledger read, without forwarding that header.

The live box in each language refreshes on page load, attempted checks, visibility and the next UTC midnight. The accessible meter includes reservations. Below $0.10 it shows “Almost used up” / “預算即將用完”. Daily stops disable submission and show the next UTC reset. Lifetime/provider stops show a pause without promising a midnight restart. Unavailable budgets disable submission until refreshed successfully.

## Atomic cost cap

One Python process and one replica use a PVC-backed SQLite ledger with one JSON state row, WAL and `synchronous=FULL`. Every read/check/write, including prune, holds a process-wide `asyncio.Lock` and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A reservation commits before every model fetch, including repairs. The [Deployment](../deploy/k8s/live-check.yaml) uses **replicas=1, strategy=Recreate**; no multi-worker server or HPA is supported.

Both caps use integer nano-USD: holds round up and caps round down. Reconciliation updates the reservation's UTC start day and lifetime counter atomically. Missing/invalid usage, failed fetches and cancellation retain the entire ceiling. Settlement is idempotent. Usage above the reservation closes the daily budget and latches the lifetime stop. A lifetime stop remains latched even if a later settlement refunds reserved cost. Increasing a limit or restarting cannot clear it.

There is **no reset endpoint or reset setting** in the self-hosted adapter. `BUDGET_RESET_ID` is ignored. Never replace/delete the PVC or reset lifetime counters to bypass a stop. Periodic pruning runs every 60 seconds; transitions also prune expired buckets. Day/hold rows expire after 48 hours, accepted-rate buckets after ten minutes and failed-auth buckets after 15 minutes. Lifetime totals, pause flags and the HMAC salt remain.

Pricing and arithmetic come from the CLI ledger/provider registry. The additional conservative hold uses serialized UTF-8 bytes plus 4,096 template/control tokens and the maximum output tokens, without cached discounts. Successful verified usage reconciles using the same pricing calculation. Review model/pricing/token contract changes before enabling them. Caps cover model estimates; host/infrastructure costs are separate.

Unknown IDs return 400; unavailable/pending/tampered files return 503 without a model reservation. `/api/check` and its 600-character boundary are unchanged.

The [existing ingest code](../src/claimcheck/ingest_media.py) extracts PDF text locally, reads images with **`muse-spark-1.3`** and transcribes audio with **`muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`**, both via **provider `meta` / the Meta Model API**. Video uses ASR plus all three existing frame samples (1/6, 1/2, 5/6 of duration). OCR/ASR text is untrusted input, not SEC evidence. The text enters the unchanged live claim runner and deterministic `corrections` builder. Fixed video inputs may contain multiple readings; the 12,000-character post-ingest ceiling does not change arbitrary pasted-text limits.

The envelope adds `input: {example_id, kind, preprocessing: {model, provider, cost_usd, latency_ms}, text_read}`. Top-level cost/latency include preprocessing; preprocessing metrics are a subset, not an additional charge. Native extraction uses provider `local` and costs zero. Every OCR/ASR attempt reserves against the **same SQLite ledger before external I/O**; missing usage/errors/timeouts retain holds. OCR adds an image-patch ceiling; ASR uses rounded-second pricing. The sync ingest functions receive bridges to the async transport/gate. Cancellation aborts pending I/O and seals the bridge, so a still-decoding thread cannot start a late paid call. No automatic provider retry is enabled by the live adapter. The whole example request has **60 s**, Pages allows **65 s** including the body, and the browser allows **70 s**. The 28/25/32 s text path is unchanged.

The bilingual renderer uses text nodes for the read text and preprocessing fields. Order: **What the model read → verdict → corrected draft → SEC evidence → agent trace (collapsed)**. Saved buttons need no password and remain available at budget stops. All five ready live cards require the same password and share the five-check/ten-minute limit. Media playback needs no password. Root-relative paths work on `/zh/`; the site CSP allows media from the same origin only.

## Privacy

Authenticated, validated runs publish their input and public result in the bounded history described above, including failed/partial attempts. This is an intentional change from the original response-only storage policy. There is no application request-body/exception log. The selected verifier receives the post and necessary SEC tool results; Meta receives media for OCR/ASR regardless of verifier choice. Providers have their own policies. Spending state retains totals, stop flags, reservation IDs/amounts/status, expiries and salted HMAC IP buckets; history is a separate table in the same SQLite file. The SEC cache stores public JSON bodies only. Access/hosting metadata is outside application history storage; do not enable body tracing or diagnostic credential dumps.

The review password travels only in the POST body, is removed before the runner and is never sent to a provider, persisted in the ledger/history, echoed or logged. After successful authentication/check only, the UI stores it in `sessionStorage` for that tab; reload restores it and a 401 clears it. Blocked browser storage still permits checks. It never enters localStorage, cookies, URLs or rendered results. The password input remains masked with autocomplete off, and the form declares POST.

The [saved Apple view](site/data/live-demo.json) derives from the original [R06 result](evidence/eval-v2-2026-10-27/R06--agent@baseten.json) and [raw trace](evidence/eval-v2-2026-10-27/traces/20261028T061222Z-6f6be742.json), retaining recorded timestamps, cost and latency. Unrecorded event timestamps remain null; private reasoning is omitted. Follow the [test-record policy](TEST_RECORDS.md); do not archive arbitrary visitor posts as test cases.

## Demo video

### v001 — first end-to-end build (2:10)

Storyboard YAML → Breeze narration → Playwright recordings of the live site → Codex stills → ACE-Step music →
ffmpeg with subtitles and ducking. **Rejected:**
- The narrator sounded like a different person in every scene (voice designed per clip).
- Site recordings were too small to read; light site vs dark stills; one scene showed the Chinese explorer under
  English narration; captions collided.

### Method change (Owner)

- Animation written in HTML + CSS + JS with `seek(t)`, so any second renders exactly; Playwright renders frames;
  ffmpeg assembles with music; motion cut to the beat.
- Staged approval: **shot list → voice → 3 key frames → 2 s motion test → full render → second-AI review.**
- Acceptance criteria: product within 3 s, phone-readable text, subtitles, one voice, ≤ 3:00, built-during-the-hackathon
  statement.

### Gates

| Gate | What happened |
|---|---|
| Shot list | 10 shots, ~2:40, approved as written (`demo/SHOTLIST-v2.md`) |
| Voice | 3 candidates (seeds 1234 / 2026 / 7); Owner picked B. Locked as a clone reference; every scene is cloned from it. Voice check: minimum similarity 0.90 (threshold 0.85) |
| Music | Prompt asked for 92 BPM; ACE-Step produced ~129 BPM with drift up to 0.24 s, so motion snaps to each detected beat instead of a fixed grid |
| Key frames | Approved after 3 tweaks. Owner asked for a more dramatic false example: Tesla (+3% vs −2.9%) replaced by Apple "$416.2B in one quarter" — really the full year; the quarter was $102.5B (4×). The new example post was run through the checker first ($0.06) so the video only shows real verdicts |
| 2 s motion test | Cards hit the beat, but were too small and flipped before the narrator named each company → cues now follow the narration (silence detection per sentence, event on the next beat) |
| v002 (2:40) | Rendered. **Failed** both reviews: `'` shown in text, small labels on phones, a few reveals out of sync, a clipped table, an imprecise "+70 points", no explicit hackathon line, and a Chinese example (Meta 623 億) whose FALSE relied on strict rounding → replaced by Coca-Cola 500 億 vs $47.1B |
| v003 | 7 of 10 fixed; new issues: SEC table numbers ran together, subtitles up to 0.6 s behind narration, missing spaces after periods in headlines |
| v004 | All three fixed (two-column proof table, subtitles from the same sentence timing as motion cues, spacing). One left: two-line subtitles 45 px from the bottom edge |
| v005 | Subtitle panel resized (2 lines = 136 px) and anchored 64 px above the bottom; measured 68–78 px on every sampled frame. 2:40, −14.5 LUFS, −1.1 dBTP. **Approved by the Owner as the final video** (rebuilt byte-identical as v006 after a media-loss incident) |

### Lessons

- Lock the voice before generating any narration; per-clip voice design drifts.
- Rebuild key UI in HTML instead of recording the live page: sharper text and exact numbers.
- Drive animation from narration timing, not just the beat.
- A second, independent AI reviewer caught issues the director missed (sync, precision of labels, clipping).
- Check the delivery tolerance: −14 LUFS ±0.5 failed on an AAC encode at −14.86; ±1 LU is standard.

Final explanations follow the program verdict; the model's draft remains in the trace. 4. **Review the result.** Open the HTML report or reuse its JSON. L4 earnings-release evidence ## L4 earnings-release evidence Guidance and non-GAAP claims can use the issuer's SEC **8-K Item 2.02** or **6-K** earnings release, through SEC-indexed HTML Ex 99.1/99.2. Muse selects a candidate quote; Python rechecks the cached bytes, offsets, metric, period and numbers. A failed XBRL lookup can also trigger the same verified release route in program checks. L4 is furnished, unaudited and medium strength at most. Consolidated reported totals are also checked against XBRL; L1/L2 wins a conflict with `release_vs_filing_mismatch`. Missing outlooks and verbal ranges such as “low to mid single digits” return insufficient evidence. The [source and comparison rules](../DATA_SOURCES.md#l4-parsing-and-decision-rules) and [independent 32-claim gold builder](../../eval/l4/GOLD_REVIEW.md) describe the supported scope. After committing the gold and source fixtures, run `.venv/bin/python eval/l4/run_agent.py`; it uses Baseten's Meta Muse Spark Open, offline SEC snapshots, and one $5 budget for the entire run. Results belong in `docs/evidence/eval-l4-2026-10-29/`. The [registered L4 run](eval-l4-2026-10-29/ANALYSIS.md) scored **31/32 (96.9%; Wilson 95% CI 84.3–99.4%)**, with **0/19 false-supported** results, for **$0.7157**. Why you can trust a verdict ## Why you can trust a verdict The model must cite the numeric evidence it used. Python parses the stated number and precision, applies direction words such as “fell” or “up,” checks the comparator, and rejects missing or ambiguous evidence. Any contradicted sub-claim makes the overall result contradicted; all supported sub-claims make it supported; otherwise the result is insufficient evidence. | Comparator | Program rule | | --- | --- | | `eq` | Difference is at most the precision implied by the stated number | | `approx` (value or absolute change) | Difference is at most `max(2 × precision, 2.5% of abs(stated))` | | `approx` (percent change) | Difference is at most `max(2 × precision, 1.0 percentage point)` | | `gt`, `lt` | Strict comparison; no tolerance | | `gte`, `lte` | Equality is accepted within the stated precision | | value-claim cap | Value tolerance is additionally capped at `10% × abs(stated value)` | `history_rank` compares like periods only, includes derived Q4 values when available, and supplies the chronological window for record and first-time checks. Every factual assertion is represented as a sub-claim; assertions outside the available EDGAR checks stay unchecked. ```mermaid flowchart LR M["Model draft

Evidence you can audit ## Evidence you can audit Every number in a verdict carries its provenance ([`docs/DATA_SOURCES.md`](../DATA_SOURCES.md), [`sources/registry.yaml`](../../sources/registry.yaml)): | Level | Source | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | L1 | 10-K (annual report) | Audited; the issuer is legally liable for it | | L2 | 10-Q (quarterly report) | Reviewed, not audited | | L3 | Derived by the program | e.g. Q4 = annual − nine-month YTD; formula and source filings listed | Each fact also reports how many filings confirm it, whether a later filing revised it, and an overall strength (high / medium / low). Guidance and non-GAAP figures are outside SEC XBRL facts; eligible claims can use [L4 issuer-release evidence](../DATA_SOURCES.md#l4-parsing-and-decision-rules). Claims without a supported source or check remain `insufficient_evidence`. **The data itself is checked.** [`docs/DATA_QUALITY.md`](../DATA_QUALITY.md) runs consistency checks over 24 issuers' SEC data (quarters summing to the year, year-to-date totals, revisions). It found that **Oracle's 10-Ks filed in 2020–2022 tag full-year revenue for fiscal 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022 on the fourth-quarter period** (e.g. $39.4B for March–May 2018). The verifier excludes those rows, derives the real quarter ($11.0B) and shows the excluded row in the evidence. ![Cached SEC data quality by issuer](../figures/data-quality.svg) *Data-quality checks per issuer, SEC companyfacts snapshot 2026-10-27.*
Evaluation ## Evaluation [`eval/claims.yaml`](../../eval/claims.yaml) holds 30 claims (20 `dev`, 10 `test`) across 11 trap categories — rounded and approximate values, inequalities, year-over-year changes with direction words, YTD-vs-quarter and fiscal-vs-calendar traps, unit traps, multi-part claims, first-time records and uncheckable claims. Gold facts come from [`eval/build_gold.py`](../../eval/build_gold.py), which reads raw SEC JSON with its own code and does not import the verifier. [`eval/v2/`](../../eval/v2) scales this to 357 claims (91 `dev`, 266 `test`) across 23 companies. - **Programmatic claims:** [`generate.py`](../../eval/v2/generate.py) makes them deterministically from a fixed seed. - **Paraphrases:** [`paraphrase.py`](../../eval/v2/paraphrase.py) has Muse Spark reword claims. Rewrites that drop a number, change a period, or comment on truth instead of rewording are rejected. - **Real-world claims:** [`real.yaml`](../../eval/v2/real.yaml) records each one with source URL, tier and publication date. Claims are stored as paraphrases, never verbatim. [`build.py`](../../eval/v2/build.py) recomputes every gold answer and refuses to build if any disagrees. Each run records a manifest (code commit, model, prompts with SHA-256, data snapshot hashes, start/end time, ledger spend before and after), one trace per model call (request, raw response, reasoning tokens, cost, latency, rate-limit headers) and a report with Wilson confidence intervals, paired bootstrap intervals and McNemar tests. Prompts live in [`prompts/`](../../prompts); a test fails if they drift from the code. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m claimcheck eval run --split all \ --systems single_shot@meta,agent@meta,single_shot@baseten,agent@baseten,single_shot@fireworks,agent@fireworks \ --budget 5 --out docs/evidence/eval-/ .venv/bin/python -m claimcheck eval report --out docs/evidence/eval-/ ``` `--dry-run` prints the plan and worst-case budget without a key or network. A failed or budget-stopped pair counts as wrong and is never silently retried.
Technical notes ## Technical notes `lookup_fact` returns period type and duration. Additive flows can be derived from annual minus nine-month YTD or from YTD differences, with source components retained; EPS and share counts are not derived. Calendar labels (`2025Q3`) use SEC frames when present and dates otherwise; fiscal labels (`FY2027Q1`) are derived from each period's dates and the issuer's fiscal year-end, because SEC `fy`/`fp` describe the filing rather than the period. A quarter whose value equals its covering annual value is treated as a tagging error and excluded. The EDGAR client reads local cache files when available, sends the configured contact User-Agent for a cache miss, and records the source SHA-256 in evidence. Tool turns reserve worst-case cost before every model call, then reconcile actual usage. Incomplete responses are retried once with a doubled limit; Baseten plain JSON is schema-validated and repaired once when needed. Prompt source files live in [`prompts/`](../../prompts), and the figure builder is [`docs/scripts/make_figures.py`](../scripts/make_figures.py). This project is not investment advice.

Within tolerance is **Exact (100)**. Otherwise the bands are **Minor** (<2% / <1 pp), **Moderate** (2–<10% / 1–<5 pp), **Major** (10–50% / 5–20 pp, or wrong direction), and **Severe** (>50% / >20 pp). Otherwise the score is `max(0, 100 − 200 × relative_gap)` or `max(0, 100 − 4 × pp_gap)`, with another 30 points deducted for wrong direction (floor 0). This display signal leaves the verdict unchanged; CAN'T CHECK has no score. Existing reports can be updated offline with `claimcheck.post.refresh_evidence(report_dir)`; `python docs/scripts/build_site.py --offline` rebuilds the cards from saved checks and trace metadata without modifying the source reports.

Agentic：Muse 選擇下一步，Python 檢查答案 - **Muse 決定查什麼。** 自主選擇工具與參數：`lookup_fact`、用 `list_periods` 確認可用期間、用 `compute_change` 比較變化、用 `history_rank` 查核紀錄型主張；合格的展望與 non-GAAP 主張則使用 `find_earnings_release` 後接 `quote_release`，再引用回傳證據撰寫判定草稿。[工具定義](../../src/claimcheck/tools.py) · [公司公告工具](../../src/claimcheck/release_tools.py)。 - **Python 執行並驗證。** 計算數值、檢查期間、單位、精度、方向與證據 ID，驗證公告原始位元組及引文位置，並決定最終判定。模型呼叫前會先保留預算。[程式檢查](../../src/claimcheck/checks.py) · [公告檢查](../../src/claimcheck/release_checks.py) · [預算紀錄](../../src/claimcheck/budget.py)。 在一筆[真實 Alphabet trace](2026-10-27/20261027T222758Z-8959a100.json)中，Muse 先選擇 `lookup_fact`，再用 `history_rank` 查核「首次」的說法；Python 檢查引用證據後才回傳判定。[時序圖](../diagrams/real-run-sequence.mmd)。 ## 查核流程 1. **保留原文。** 抽出財務主張，記錄引用與可取得的頁碼、畫面或音訊位置。 2. **搜尋證據。** Meta Muse 模型選取對應公司與期間的 SEC 數值或合格公司公告。 3. **程式檢查。** Python 驗證引用、數字、單位、比較方向與四捨五入。最終摘要依程式判定產生，模型原稿另存於 trace。 4. **檢視報告。** 開啟 HTML 或重用 JSON；同一股票的多份文件可以彙整，未完成項目仍會顯示。 | 結果 | 意義 | | --- | --- | | `supported` | 在已檢查的期間與精度內，證據支持抽取出的主張。 | | `contradicted` | 有效證據與主張衝突，報告列出實際比對的數值。 | | `insufficient_evidence` | 缺少必要期間、來源或可支援的檢查，不能據此認定主張錯誤。 | 上傳文件是待查核的主張來源，不會自動成為可信的財務證據。 ## # Tesla 第 23 頁圖表診斷與改善 — 2026-10-30

結論：**圖片清楚，主要缺口是從圖形轉成有來源座標、誤差範圍的結構化主張。** 此次沒有新增付費呼叫、沒有估造柱狀圖數值，也沒有修改原 benchmark 或兩次修正實驗。

[原圖](../real-media-2026-10-30/images/tesla-q3-2026-23.png) · [原始 OCR](../fair-multimodal-v1/prepared/REAL-TSLA-23/prepared.json) · [原始抽取結果](../stock-context-posthoc-2026-10-30/attempt-2/REAL-TSLA-23/ingest.json) · [新版三文件摘要](summary/stock-review.html) · [來源雜湊與機器診斷](diagnosis.json)

## 圖片具體有什麼問題？

本次直接檢視 1800 × 1013 的原圖並與保存的 OCR 比對；這是個案診斷，不是獨立人工標註集或新的準確率評測。

| 圖表 | 圖上能讀到 | 不能從 OCR 取得的關係 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 左：Vehicle Deliveries | 季度、0.0–0.5 刻度、單位 millions of units | 每根柱子對應的實際交付量；柱上沒有數字標籤 |
| 中：Operating / Free Cash Flow | 季度、-3–7 刻度、兩種圖例、單位 $B | 顏色與序列、柱高／負柱、每季度各項數值 |
| 右：Net Income / Adjusted EBITDA | 季度、0–8 刻度、圖例與 $B | 每根柱與序列的對應，精確值及 GAAP／non-GAAP 語意 |

圖片不需要先歸因於模糊或解析度不足：可見的季度、圖例、刻度與三則註腳已進入 OCR。**座標上的 7、6、5 是刻度，不能當成某季現金流。** 原圖沒有逐柱精確數字；放大或裁切可以協助定位，但無法憑空增加不存在的標籤。

保存的文字沒有柱子的邊界座標、顏色或高度，所以後續文字模型失去圖形關係。股票提示模式的抽取規則也明確禁止從柱／線位置猜數字；零主張符合這個保守契約。這不是圖片內容已被驗證，也不能由此推論模型永遠不會讀圖。程式狀態 `completed` 只表示流程結束；查核階段實際未到達。

三則註腳還包含資本支出呈現調整、2024 年季度重列、Adjusted EBITDA 排除數位資產損益。即使能量出高度，也必須對齊這份簡報的重列版本與季度口徑；非 GAAP EBITDA 不能直接當成 SEC 淨利。

## 此次已改善

1. 每個 OCR channel 明確揭露：文字查核沒有驗證柱高、線條、顏色或序列與季度對應。即使同圖的文字主張查核成功，這項限制仍存在。
2. 分別提示「沒有讀到文字」、「有文字但零主張」、「處理錯誤」。不會把所有零主張都自動診斷成圖表，也不把處理錯誤當成成功拒答。
3. 單檔報告及股票彙整都附上可執行的補救：提供對應數值表、單位、期間和註腳；檢視原始 trace 後才考慮付費重跑。
4. 用原來三份 Tesla 結果重新產生新版摘要，保留原始報告雜湊與連結。仍是三筆 supported、五筆 insufficient；圖表頁沒有新增已驗證主張。這是診斷呈現改善，**尚未完成自動圖形數值驗證**。

[驗證紀錄](verification.log)與[重播檢查](replay.log)保留在此目錄。新增五項離線測試涵蓋真實圖表重播、成功文字不代表幾何正確、錯誤優先、空文字及 HTML 安全轉義。使用 `uv run python scripts/replay_chart_diagnosis.py`（使用 repo 鎖定依賴） 可重播；不讀 API key、不需要 SEC 網路請求。既有付費輸入輸出保持原樣，新增 API 費用 $0。

## 下一步：依實用性及可驗證性排序

| 順位 | 要做的事 | 通過條件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | 同股票多文件中，把圖表與同份官方簡報的數值表建立候選關聯；先要求人工確認 | 每項有公司、季度、單位、GAAP／non-GAAP、文件版本和頁碼；確認表格數字不代表圖形已正確 |
| P1 | 擴充季度營運現金流及交付量等證據來源 | 年初累計不能直接當單季；計算差額需同版本證據及完整算式；非 GAAP 須保留定義與調節表 |
| P2 | 新增可選原生視覺結構抽取：圖框、軸、序列、柱框、季度、單位、註腳 | 同圖／同 prompt 三平台比較，保存完整 input/output；圖形估值須獨立標為 approximate，不能冒充原文精確引述 |
| P2 | 幾何讀值與區間判定 | 依刻度、像素誤差與圖形品質建立區間，處理負值、截斷軸、對數軸；與證據相交僅算區間相容，不宣稱精確值相等 |
| P3 | 擴大盲測及錯誤圖表組 | 多公司、重列、雙軸、堆疊、遮擋、誤導刻度；獨立標註＋保留測試組；分開公布抽取覆蓋、數值誤差及錯誤支持率 |

評審展示目前應說：「能指出哪份文件沒有完成查核及原因，並引導補齊資料。」在 P2 通過前，不能說「已能驗證所有財報圖表」。本次不再花額度重跑純 OCR，因為那不會補上缺失的圖形表示；後續實驗應另存新版本並明確限定預算。

- 開發組是 Apple、Nvidia，每家公司四個主張，測試查核階段的預設／低推理兩個設定。短文件抽取仍沿用原 repo 的預設推理，並沒有自動繼承查核的 low 設定；完整 request 可查證。依正確數、錯誤支持數、成本選擇；三家最後都選到低推理。這是「兩個開發設定中較好的選擇」，不是宣稱已找到模型所有可能配置中的最佳值。
- 正式組是 Amazon、Intel、Tesla、Microsoft、Alphabet、Meta。每家公司四個主張：兩個真實數值、一個故意改錯的淨利，以及一個截至日尚無證據的未來期間。
- 同一內容轉成 TXT、Markdown、原生文字 PDF、PNG、JPEG、WebP、WAV、MP3、MP4。**只有 24 個獨立的基礎主張、六個公司群組**；格式轉換不能變成 216 個獨立題目來縮小誤差。
- 三家使用同一份檔案、同一份截至 2026-10-30 的 SEC 快照、固定輸出上限及評分規則。Meta 是 Muse Spark 1.3；Baseten、Fireworks 是指定的 Muse Spark Open 端點，因此結果同時包含模型與服務差異。這是 repo 已整合的 Muse 模型比較，不是各平台所有模型的排行榜。

## 為什麼分成兩種比較

**產品流程測試**先共用並凍結 Meta OCR／ASR 結果，再讓三家查核完全相同的文字。這能比較「這個產品搭配哪個文字查核平台」，不能證明另外兩家原生處理聲音或影片的能力。

**原生圖片測試**則把相同 PNG、JPEG、WebP 直接送給各家的圖片端點。數字保存率、文字編輯率只是辨識診斷，不是財務判斷正確率，也不是圖片真偽檢查。這些原生圖片呼叫只屬於測試工具；產品 `ingest` 仍共用 Meta OCR，並未因此新增另一條原生圖片查核流程。原生聲音／影片端點本輪沒有測試，應標示未測，不應寫成不支援。

三張真實 Tesla 投影片另列診斷。它們沒有完整、獨立人工審核的標準答案，因此不混入準確率分母。控制組的音訊是 eSpeak 合成語音，影片是靜態卡片加語音，不能推論到真實長時間法說會、快速變換的畫面或說話者身分辨識。

## 準確率、速度與價格怎麼看

1. 嚴格正確率包含所有預先列出的主張；漏抽、對不到公司／指標／期間、未完成與判錯都會扣分。不能只對成功抽出的句子計算準確率。
2. 「錯誤支持」另外顯示：錯誤或缺乏證據的主張被判為 supported，與保守拒答是不同問題。拒答仍會在應有答案的題目扣分。
3. 相同文字的查核結果可以用雜湊快取重用，但每次重用都標示來源。它不是新的模型實驗，快取命中也不拿來宣稱 API 比較快。
4. 三家的實際使用／保留額包含開發、失敗、診斷與原生圖片呼叫；共用 OCR／ASR 費用全記在 Meta。每份文件的工作流程估算成本另列，不能把它們全部相加再當成實際帳單。
5. 延遲只反映這次固定並行度與網路下的觀察，不是服務 SLA。六個公司群組的信賴區間也很不穩定，不能推出全面的供應商排名。這是單次實驗，尚未量測重複推理的波動；公司群組 bootstrap 也不涵蓋模型隨機性。高分主要反映清晰的單一數值題，不代表複雜金融敘事、因果解釋或預測的正確率。
6. 每平台授權上限是 $40，呼叫准入上限設為 $35 留下結算餘裕。這是支出上限，不是必須花完的額度；ledger 是估算／保留額，尚未與供應商帳單核銷。

## 本輪結論與已完成的修正

正式九種格式中，Fireworks 每種皆為 24/24；Baseten 除 WAV 23/24 外皆為 24/24；Meta 介於 MP3 的 14/24 與 PNG 的 24/24。這表示在這份小型控制組與固定流程中，Fireworks 的完整度最高，不能據此宣稱所有金融資料都能百分之百驗證。三家沒有觀察到錯誤支持，但底層負面／證據不足題目只有 12 個，並非零風險證明。

每家 42 個非快取文字工作（抽取加多次查核）的中位時間：Meta 123.222 秒、Baseten 25.635 秒、Fireworks 165.021 秒；不含共用 OCR／ASR。Baseten 在這次環境較快，Fireworks 完整率較高。Meta 的落差包含抽取未完成、額外子主張未驗證與保守拒答，不能直接歸因於聲音辨識品質。各平台原生 PNG、JPEG、WebP 都完成各 6/6 個控制圖片；數字 token 保存率皆為 72/72，但這項正規化指標不驗證正負號、單位綁定或表格語意。

真實 Tesla 三頁在原始流程中全部未產生可用主張，這個失敗已原樣保留。之後另開 [產品修正實驗](../stock-context-posthoc-2026-10-30/REPORT.md)：加入未經認證的股票代號提示、有限主張抽取及連續原文列引用。第一輪仍有四筆非連續引用被拒絕；第二輪保留八個主張，三筆有證據、五筆證據不足，圖表頁零主張仍標示未查核。[實際摘要](../stock-context-posthoc-2026-10-30/attempt-2/summary/stock-review.html)可以直接開啟。

這是已知失敗上的 Baseten 修正檢查，重用原有 Meta OCR，沒有重新估計三家準確率，也沒有改寫原始 benchmark。新增的股票提示不能覆蓋文件明示的其他公司。現金流指標與營運 KPI 的證據覆蓋仍不足；此輪也沒有修正 Meta 的未知子主張合併規則。

全部支出估算／保留額：Meta $4.23601935、Baseten $2.09934800、Fireworks $2.01364550。Baseten 包含另外兩輪合計 $0.14738175；每家皆低於 $40。費用不是帳戶剩餘 credit，也不是供應商最終帳單。[機器可讀總帳](task-spend.json)與兩套稽核分開保留。

已完成 CLI 多文件查核、可追溯摘要及 901 個產品測試；下一個產品優先項目是多檔上傳介面，再來才是有引用與數值校驗的 AI 敘述摘要。真實人工標註資料及現金流／營運指標覆蓋應同步擴充，使用新的保留測試組評估。

# Live check implementation verification

2026-11-02, branch `site/live-check-trace`. No push, deployment, Cloudflare secret access, paid model call, or live SEC fetch was performed. The [implementation and handoff](../../LIVE_CHECK.md) describe the optional production setup.

## Final validation

[`UV_OFFLINE=1 sh scripts/verify.sh`](verification-final.log) **passed** with 962 product/replay/provider/site tests, 149 demo tests and 55 standalone Node tests. It also rebuilt/checked figures, reproduced all three explorer/site/build-summary outputs byte for byte, and passed Markdown links/anchors with network guards active. The full verifier needed no key, live SEC data, Wrangler or npm install.

[Focused tests](focused-tests.log) include source identity, all 357 v2 Baseten tool transcripts, real Apple raw-response replay, three outcomes, missing-period abstention, failed-call accounting, concurrent reservations, idempotent settlement, integer money, cross-midnight rate windows, safe DOM rendering, both languages, and the Pages boundary. [Input/source hashes](inputs.json) identify the implementation, reused trace and SEC fixtures. These tests compare the live finish path to the same Python CLI checker; they do not port or substitute verdict logic.

[The Python Worker dry run](worker-dry-run.log) bundled successfully with Wrangler 4.156.2; the final Pages Function bundle also compiled successfully. No deployment occurred. Local `wrangler pages dev` returned HTTP 200 / `mode=mock` for the exact saved Apple input, with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

[The isolated Python/WASM smoke](worker-smoke.json) used the production runner and real SQLite Durable Object, replacing **only** model and SEC transports with recorded responses/fixtures. It returned `supported`, seven public trace events and replayed usage cost $0.01221725. **New paid cost: $0.** A missing-period sentence returned `insufficient_evidence` with zero model cost. Five requests from one test IP succeeded; the sixth returned 429 / `rate_limited`. Setting the isolated Worker's budget to zero returned 429 / `budget_exhausted` before model transport. The smoke JSON wraps the normal `mode=live` service response in an explicit `offline_runtime_replay` label; it is not a fresh live-model run.

The frontend skill's source lint passed with zero failures/warnings. DOM/runtime checks cover phone/tablet/desktop widths and EN/中文; the new form/trace has no animation and uses the existing light/dark variables. **Real-browser screenshots and visual approval were not completed:** the inspector's Chrome process exited in the sandbox, browser-host access was unavailable, and native computer-use access to Google Chrome was denied. Claude/owner should do the browser checks in the deployment handoff. Production model latency, SEC egress and cold-start behavior remain unmeasured; the 30-second target is bounded by timeout behavior, not a production SLA claim.

三家各查核同樣六個已凍結的主張，沒有重跑語音辨識、OCR 或抽取。這是上一輪已知失敗的事後產品驗證，不是獨立準確率評測。[完整結果](REPORT.md) · [可讀報告](results.html) · [原始輸入與來源](cases.json)。
